key_insight: The CALPHAD-based Gamma metric correlates better with tensile ductility than the DFT-based D-parameter while performing equally well in compression for refractory compositionally complex alloys.
engineering_relevance: Gamma could help screen refractory alloys for room-temperature ductility alongside the high-temperature performance needed in extreme environments.
method: Combine BCC–HCP free-energy differences, (110) BCC surface interfacial free energy, and electronegativity-corrected lattice distortion into Gamma.
Compare ductility correlations against established semi-empirical metrics and the DFT-based D-parameter.
Propose pairing Gamma with CALPHAD-calculated oxygen solubility to address intrinsic and extrinsic brittleness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a modest improvement in tensile-ductility correlation over the D-parameter and equal performance in compression, without quantitative evaluation details.
watch_item: The oxygen-solubility extension is a proposed first-order approach, not an established predictor of oxygen-induced embrittlement.
paper_title: Thermodynamic Underpinnings Affecting Compressive and Tensile Plasticity in Refractory Compositionally Complex Alloys
